title: The Dome, the Crab and the Gold Pen

bands.1:
It is Thursday night. Tomorrow, Maxx's divers will come for Clawsette. Tonight, the crew goes first.

You all slip into the dark water. Captain Clause swims beside you in an old brass helmet.

Tully leads the way. "Left at the brain coral," she whispers. "Right at the coral shaped like a footy."

Mo stays on the boat to cook prawn jelly. That is scarier than the heist.

The gold dome glows ahead. Zed types MAXXISGREAT. Beep. Wrong. He types ILOVEME. The door slides open.

"Easiest hack ever," says Zed.

Inside, there are rows of glass tanks. A Kelpwick. A Tocktle. A Mendlet with four arms. The labels say, "RESCUED (LOL)."

A camera drone buzzes over. Gus throws a blob of green goo. Splat! The drone is stuck to the ceiling.

"Snot-Glue," says Gus proudly. "Made from whale snot. That's not gross. That's science."

Clawsette snips the locks. Snip, snip, snip. The Biffoon punches its own tank open.

You find a gold desk. On it is a list in gold pen. It is Maxx's Wishlist. Every rare Creature on the reef is ticked. At the bottom it says, "Clawsette. LAST ONE! Get her Friday."

"Proof," you say.

"He always uses a gold pen," says Wren. Then she adds, "I bet."

Then the Kelpwick sneezes. A big bubble pops on the alarm. Gold lights flash.

"Smash that alarm button!" yells a recording of Maxx.

"Go!" you shout.

Captain Clause holds the door. Gus glues it shut behind you.

Back on the boat, Captain Clause turns the Wishlist over. On the back, it says, "THE BIG ONE: Old Glimmer. Live finale."

Captain Clause goes pale. "Old Glimmer is real," he whispers. "She is the giant glowing ray from the old stories. Nobody has seen her in fifty years. And Maxx is hunting her."
bands.2:
It's Thursday night. Tomorrow, Maxx's divers are coming for Clawsette. So tonight, the crew is going first.

You all slip into the black water. Captain Clause swims beside you in an old brass diving helmet, and Clawsette rides on top of it like a tiny general.

Tully leads the way through the coral. "Left at the brain coral," she whispers. "Then right at the coral shaped like a footy."

Mo has stayed on the boat as the getaway driver. He is also making prawn jelly, which might be more dangerous than the heist.

The gold dome glows ahead. Indi has painted "POD CLEANING CREW" on everyone's wetsuits, and the letters are already running. There's a keypad by the door. Zed types MAXXISGREAT. Beep. Wrong. He tries ILOVEME, and the door slides open.

"Easiest hack of my life," says Zed.

Inside, rows of glass tanks glow in the dark. Each tank holds a Creature: a Kelpwick, a Tocktle, a Mendlet with only four arms. Each one has a gold label that says, "RESCUED (LOL)."

A camera drone buzzes towards you, its red light blinking. Gus flings a blob of green goo. Splat! The drone is glued to the ceiling.

"Snot-Glue," says Gus proudly. "Made from real whale snot. That's not gross. That's science."

Clawsette snips the tank locks one by one. Wren lifts each Creature out gently, whispering to it. The Biffoon doesn't wait. It punches its own tank open.

At the back of the dome, you find a gold desk. On it is a list written in gold pen: Maxx's Wishlist. Every rare Creature on the reef has been ticked off. At the bottom it says, "Clawsette. LAST ONE! Get her Friday."

"That's our proof," you say, rolling it up.

"He always ticks things in gold pen," says Wren. Then she quickly adds, "I mean, I bet he does."

Then the Kelpwick sneezes. A big bubble floats up and pops on the alarm. Gold lights start flashing.

"Smash that alarm button!" yells a recording of Maxx.

"Go!" you shout.

Everyone swims for the door with the Creatures. Captain Clause holds it open with his huge arms, and Gus glues it shut behind you.

Back on the Soggy Biscuit, dripping and grinning, Captain Clause turns the Wishlist over. On the back, in big gold letters, it says, "THE BIG ONE: Old Glimmer. Live finale."

Captain Clause goes pale. "Old Glimmer is real," he whispers. "The giant glowing ray from the old stories. Nobody has seen her in fifty years. And Maxx is hunting her."
bands.3:
It's Thursday night. Tomorrow, Maxx's divers are coming for Clawsette, so tonight the crew is going in first.

One by one, you slip into the black water. Captain Clause, who has given you his badge and his trust, swims beside you in an old brass diving helmet. Clawsette rides on top of it like a tiny general leading an army.

Tully leads the way through the coral, counting fins. "Left at the brain coral," she whispers into her mask. "Then right at the coral shaped like a footy."

Mo has stayed on the boat as the getaway driver. He is also making prawn jelly, which might be more dangerous than the heist itself.

The gold dome glows ahead of you. Indi has painted "POD CLEANING CREW" across everyone's wetsuits, and the letters are already starting to run. There's a keypad beside the airlock door. Zed types MAXXISGREAT. Beep. Wrong. He tries ILOVEME, and the door hisses open.

"Easiest hack of my entire life," Zed mutters.

Inside, rows of glass tanks glow in the darkness. Each tank holds a Creature: a Kelpwick with drooping fronds, a Tocktle whose clock has stopped, a Mendlet with only four arms. Every tank has a gold label that says, "RESCUED (LOL)."

A camera drone buzzes towards you, its red light blinking. Before it can film a thing, Gus flings a blob of green goo. Splat! The drone is glued to the ceiling, its propellers whining.

"Snot-Glue," says Gus proudly. "Made from genuine whale snot. That's not gross. That's science."

Clawsette scuttles along the tanks, snipping each lock with a neat click. Wren lifts each Creature out gently, murmuring to it as if it were a baby. The Biffoon doesn't wait for anyone. It punches its own tank open and swims out looking pleased with itself.

At the back of the dome, you find a gold desk. On it lies a list written in gold pen: Maxx's Wishlist. Every rare Creature on the reef has been ticked off in curly handwriting. At the bottom it says, "Clawsette. LAST ONE! Get her Friday."

"That's our proof," you say, rolling it up and tucking it into your waterproof bag.

"He always ticks things off in gold pen," says Wren. Then she quickly adds, "I mean, I bet he does."

Then the Kelpwick sneezes. An enormous bubble wobbles upwards and pops right on the alarm sensor. Gold lights start flashing everywhere.

"Smash that alarm button like it owes you money!" yells a recording of Maxx.

"Go!" you shout.

Everyone swims for the airlock, towing the Creatures with them. Captain Clause holds the heavy door open with his huge arms while Gus glues it shut behind you.

Back on the Soggy Biscuit, dripping and grinning, Captain Clause turns the Wishlist over. On the back, in big gold letters, it says, "THE BIG ONE: Old Glimmer. Live finale."

Captain Clause's face goes pale under his beard. "Old Glimmer is real," he whispers. "The great glowing ray from the old sea stories. Nobody has seen her in fifty years. And Maxx is hunting her."
bands.4:
It is Thursday night. Tomorrow, Maxx's divers are coming for Clawsette, which is why, tonight, the crew is going in first.

One by one, you slip over the side into the inky water. Captain Clause, who has finally given you his badge and, more slowly, his trust, swims beside you in an ancient brass diving helmet, with Clawsette riding on top of it like a very small general leading a very large invasion.

Tully leads the way through the coral, counting fins and checking her compass. "Left at the brain coral," she whispers into her mask. "Then right at the coral shaped like a footy."

"Which footy?" asks Zed.

"A Reef Rays footy. Obviously. It's the one that looks like it's losing."

Mo has stayed aboard the Soggy Biscuit as getaway driver, where he is also experimenting with prawn jelly. Of the two jobs, only one is likely to hurt anybody.

The gold dome glows ahead of you, humming faintly. Indi has painted "POD CLEANING CREW" across everyone's wetsuits, and the letters are already beginning to dribble. Beside the airlock is a keypad. Zed types MAXXISGREAT and gets a sulky beep, then tries ILOVEME, and the door hisses open with a sigh of bubbles.

"That's not even a boss level," Zed mutters. "That's the tutorial."

Wren stays a moment longer, looking at the keypad as though it has told her something she already knew. "He never could think of one that wasn't about himself," she says, so quietly that only you hear it.

Inside, rows of glass tanks glow in the dark, and in each one floats a Creature that ought to be out on the reef: a Kelpwick with drooping fronds, a Tocktle whose clock hands have stopped, a Mendlet with only four of its arms still waving. Every tank wears the same gold label: "RESCUED (LOL)."

A camera drone whirs towards you, red light blinking. Before it can film a single frame, Gus flings a blob of green goo, and the drone is cemented to the ceiling, propellers whining.

"Snot-Glue," says Gus. "Genuine whale snot. Harvested by me, personally."

"Harvested how?" asks Tully.

Gus, wisely, does not answer.

Clawsette scuttles along the tanks, snipping each lock with a neat click, while Wren lifts the Creatures out one at a time and murmurs to each as if it were a baby. The Biffoon, who has never in its life waited for anybody, punches its own tank open and swims out looking enormously pleased with itself.

At the back of the dome stands a gold desk, a gold chair and, for reasons nobody can explain, a gold rubbish bin. On the desk lies a list in gold pen: Maxx's Wishlist. Every rare Creature on the reef is there, ticked off in loopy, show-off handwriting, and at the very bottom, in bigger letters than the rest: "Clawsette. LAST ONE! Get her Friday."

"Clawsette," says Captain Clause, reading it over your shoulder. "Last one." He scowls. "That is not a sentence. That is a crumb. Who is getting her, and when?"

"Nobody," you say, rolling the list up inside your waterproof bag. "Not now."

"Gold pen," says Wren softly, to nobody in particular. Then, a little too quickly: "People like him always use gold pen. I bet."

At that exact moment, the Kelpwick sneezes. A bubble the size of a beach ball wobbles upwards, pops directly on the alarm sensor, and the whole dome erupts in flashing gold light.

"Smash that alarm button like it owes you money!" yells a recording of Maxx, from speakers you hadn't noticed.

"Go!" you shout.

Everyone kicks for the airlock, towing the Creatures behind them. Captain Clause braces the heavy door with both arms while Gus slaps a last glob of Snot-Glue across the frame, sealing it shut behind you.

Back on the Soggy Biscuit, dripping and shivering and unable to stop grinning, the crew collapses on the deck. Below the boat, the freed Creatures spiral back into the coral, flashing every colour of the reef. Mo offers round a tray of prawn jelly, and not even the Biffoon is brave enough.

Captain Clause, meanwhile, has turned the Wishlist over. On the back, in letters twice the size of anything on the front, Maxx has written: "THE BIG ONE: Old Glimmer. Live finale."

The old captain does not say anything for a long time, which, for a man who corrects other people's sentences, is the most frightening thing you have seen him do.

"Old Glimmer," he says at last, "is real. The great glowing ray from the old sea stories, as wide as a reef. Nobody has seen her in fifty years." He folds the list very small. "And Maxx is hunting her."
